definition: The small module (linear layer, MLP, or resampler like Q-Former) mapping vision-encoder outputs into the LLM's token space, aligning the two pretrained components with modest training (the LLaVA recipe).
details: The small module (linear layer, MLP, or resampler like Q-Former) mapping vision-encoder outputs into the LLM's token space, aligning the two pretrained components with modest training (the LLaVA recipe).

explainer.lead: A projector is the small module mapping vision-encoder outputs into the LLM's token space, aligning two pretrained components with modest training. It matters because this alignment step is what lets a vision model and a language model work together.

tiers.eli5: It's a translator that turns what a computer "sees" into the kind of words a language model understands, so the two parts can talk to each other.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers implement it as a linear layer, an MLP, or a resampler such as Q-Former, following the LLaVA recipe of training only this module to align a frozen vision encoder with an LLM. A pitfall is that the projector's quality bounds how well visual information reaches the language model.
tiers.paperLevel: The projector is a small module (linear layer, MLP, or resampler like Q-Former) mapping vision-encoder outputs into the LLM's token space, aligning the two pretrained components with modest training in the LLaVA recipe. A known limit is that alignment depends on this lightweight module.

explainer.example: In the LLaVA recipe, a vision encoder's outputs pass through a small MLP projector that turns them into tokens the language model can consume.
